title: Brake Wear Rate and Late Warning of Wear Limits on the Northern Winter Network
abstract: Operator request covering a brake wear rate roughly a third above the published figure on short cold-weather sectors, and a wear indication that reaches the limit between checks without any useful warning beforehand.

sections.request: We fly short sectors into cold, contaminated runways and we are getting about a third less life out of a brake than the figures we planned around. That we could live with. What we cannot live with is that the wear indication tells us nothing useful until it is almost at the limit, and then it tells us all at once. Twice this winter we have had an aircraft arrive at an outstation with a brake at the limit, no spare within four hundred kilometres, and an overnight cancellation as a result. Our people say the pin reading is fine at the last check and out of limits at the next one, with nothing in between. We want either a brake that lasts longer on our sort of operation or a way of knowing three or four weeks in advance that one is coming due, and honestly we would take the warning over the extra life.
sections.background: We have been through this with our previous fleet and the answer there was a wear count computed from the brake applications and the energy, published at every landing. We understand this aircraft counts the applications already for other purposes. We have not asked for a heavier brake because our sector length means we would carry the weight for nothing on most flights. We have kept our own wear log at every turn on three aircraft for a season and can make it available.
sections.expected_outcome: A predictive wear figure the maintenance system can read off the aircraft, ideally with the remaining landings estimated, and if it can be had at the same time a heat stack that suits high-cycle cold operation. A retrofit that can be done at a line stop would be worth far more to us than a better one that needs the aircraft in the hangar.

type_data.business_justification: Two overnight cancellations at outstations in one winter, brake life about 32 per cent below the published figure on the operator's sector mix, and no usable advance warning of a wear limit between scheduled checks.
